#### Predictions

1. With your chosen league, predict the probabilities of the first week of the season. Use distribution approach. (4p)

```{r}
week1 <- read.csv('Italy.csv')
head(week1)
```

Probabilities

```{r}
h_g <- f_data_sm %>% filter(COUNTRY=='Italy', SEASON == 2019) %>% group_by(HOMETEAM) %>% 
  summarise(mean.h = mean(FTHG))
a_g <- f_data_sm %>% filter(COUNTRY=='Italy', SEASON == 2019) %>% group_by(AWAYTEAM) %>% 
  summarise(mean.a = mean(FTAG))
```

## JOining with week1

```{r}
df <- dplyr::left_join(week1, h_g, by = 'HOMETEAM')
df <- dplyr::left_join(df, a_g, by = 'AWAYTEAM')
df <- na.omit(df)
```

### Define a function

```{r}
probs <- function(mean.h, away.h){
  rs <- rskellam(10000,mu1 = mean.h, mu2 = away.h)
  HTW <- sum(rs>0)/10000
  D <- sum(rs == 0)/10000
  ATW <- sum(rs<0)/10000
  result <- c(HTW, D, ATW)
  return(result)
}

probs(df$mean.h[2], df$mean.a[2])

```



2. Now use Poisson regression for the same task as above. Create the model and predict the probabilities. Interpret the home team coefficient. (6p)

# Data preperation

```{r}
seriea <- f_data_sm %>%
            filter(SEASON==2019, COUNTRY=="Italy") %>%
            select(HOMETEAM, AWAYTEAM, FTHG, FTAG)

s1 <- data.frame(seriea[,c("HOMETEAM", "AWAYTEAM", "FTHG")], Home=1)
s2 <- data.frame(seriea[,c("AWAYTEAM", "HOMETEAM", "FTAG")], Home=0)
colnames(s1) <- c("Team", "Opponent", "Goal", "Home")
colnames(s2) <- c("Team", "Opponent","Goal", "Home")
seriea2 <- rbind(s1, s2)
head(seriea2)
```

# Model

```{r}
model_sa<-glm(Goal~Team+Opponent+Home, data=seriea2, family=poisson(link=log))

```


# Probalities


Data prep for week1

```{r}
s1 <- data.frame(df[,c("HOMETEAM", "AWAYTEAM")], Home=1)
s2 <- data.frame(df[,c("AWAYTEAM", "HOMETEAM")], Home=0)
colnames(s1) <- c("Team", "Opponent", "Home")
colnames(s2) <- c("Team", "Opponent", "Home")
week1_p <- rbind(s1, s2)
```



```{r}
means_pred <- predict(model_sa, week1_p, type = 'response')
df$h_poisson <- means_pred[1:7]
df$a_poisson <- means_pred[8:14]
df
```

### Bradley terry model

You need to construct Bradley-Terry model for NBA regular season games. Dataset is nba2009_2018 from SportsAnalytics270 package 

Remove the game Boston Celtics vs Indiana Pacers from the dataframe. This is a game that was cancelled due to Boston Marathon bombing

```{r}
data("nba2009_2018")
nba2009_2018 <- nba2009_2018 %>%  filter(home.PTS !=0)
```

1. Do the Data Prep here (4p)

```{r}
nba <- nba2009_2018 %>%
  select(home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME, home.WL) %>%
  mutate(ht_w = ifelse(home.WL == "W",1,0),
         at_w = ifelse(home.WL== "L",1,0))

nba2 <- nba %>%
    mutate(team_home=as.factor(home.TEAM_NAME),
           team_away = as.factor(away.TEAM_NAME)) %>%
    group_by(home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME) %>%
    summarise(ht=sum(ht_w), at=sum(at_w))

# prepare for the home team advantage

nba2$home.TEAM_NAME <- data.frame(team = nba2$home.TEAM_NAME, at.home = 1)
nba2$away.TEAM_NAME <- data.frame(team = nba2$away.TEAM_NAME, at.home = 0)
```

2. Model here (4p)

```{r}
model <- BTm(cbind(ht, at), home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME, formula=~team+at.home,
            data=nba2, id="team")
```


3. Plot the abilities: Which team is the beast, which the worst ? (4p)

```{r}
abilities <- as.data.frame(BTabilities(model))
abilities$team <- rownames(abilities)
abilities <- abilities[order(abilities$ability, decreasing = T),]

ggplot(data=abilities, aes(x=reorder(team, ability), y=ability)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill=1:30) + coord_flip()+
  labs(x="Teams", y="Ability to Win", title="Ability to win of NFL teams")
```
